preparation_detail: decapitated adult females, groups of 5-10 on paper on a hot plate, filmed from above at 60 fps
effector: LexAop-TRPA1 (dTRPA1), heat ramp 24 to 37 °C over ~50 s
penetrance: distance walked ranged from just over one body length to more than ten body lengths; takeoff 'rarely'
coverage_notes: Supp. file 1 off-target: '10-20 neurons in abdominal neuromeres'. Discussion: 'In all cases, the predominant expression in the line was from the target hemilineage.'
locator: Results, section 'Hemilineages 1A and 1B', PDF p. 8; Figure 4D and legend (p. 9); Video 2 legend and frame montage v002; Figure 9A row 1A (p. 26); Supplementary file 1 row 1A
quote: Activation of 1A interneurons via TRPA1 evoked forward locomotion. As the temperature ramped up, the decapitated flies started to walk
other_observation: Locomotion occasionally interrupted by grooming bouts; leg movements erratic, not in tripod gait, 'but there was clear intersegmental coordination of the limbs'; net movement always forwards; 'Rarely, a fly would takeoff during the heat ramp.'
notes: d2-d4 yes from 'clear intersegmental coordination of the limbs' (the limbs = all legs). d5/d6/d7 no: Figure 9A shows no bar for 1A in the posture-change or uncoordinated-leg columns. d11-d13 unclear: Figure 9A shows only small marks in the wing-wave and wing-buzz columns for 1A, and the text does not mention wing movements; I could not resolve them at the available image resolution. d10 yes from text, consistent with a small Figure 9A takeoff mark.
